#2837. Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac rally as Ackman presses for conservatorship exit

The midterm elections could be a turning point for the release of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac from government control, according to billionaire investor Bill Ackman.

Investors may agree with him, if the rally in both stocks is any sign.

The Federal National Mortgage Association, known as Fannie Mae, and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, or Freddie Mac, have each jumped more than 60% from Oct. 14 to Monday's close. The stocks were both up roughly 3% on Tuesday.

Ackman, the founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, has long pushed for the two entities to be released from federal conservatorship.

"The reason why it's not being touched right now is, you know, midterms," he said in an interview with CNBC's "Squawk Box."

Ackman, who owns both names through Pershing Square, believes Freddie and Fannie have the potential to increase "10-fold from current share prices," he said in his quarterly letter to shareholders, issued on Monday.

Fannie and Freddie buy mortgages from banks and other lenders, and then package them into mortgage-backed securities, known as MBS. Their operations are critical to the housing market, providing liquidity to banks and creating a secondary market for MBS.

The entities were placed into conservatorship in September 2008, during the financial crisis. The stocks were delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in 2010 and have traded over the counter since then.

Ackman wants the conservatorship to end, arguing the entities would be worth multiples of their current valuation if they were freed from government control.

President Donald Trump has supported ending the conservatorship of Fannie and Freddie. But it remains politically and economically contentious.

The entities operate under strict capital threshold requirements and would need to be recapitalized, which could happen through issuing common equity. However, the Treasury Department would need to figure out an exit plan for its roughly $388 billion ownership stake in the entities through preferred securities and warrants.

Congress may also need to play a role, passing legislation to restructure the government's role in mortgage financing and home-loan guarantees.

Nonetheless, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently said it could happen before Trump's term ends, telling 2Way's "The Morning Meeting" podcast that the administration will tackle the ownership structure "next year, the year after." He said affordability will be guiding the decision.

One point of controversy is whether ending the conservatorship of Fannie and Freddie would increase the spreads on MBS over Treasuries, effectively making mortgages costlier. Bessent has sought to reassure the market that wouldn't happen.

"Whatever we do is going to be guided by making sure that the spread on [agency] mortgages … over the Treasury does not increase," Bessent said.

Ackman argues that privatizing the GSEs would help insulate them from political meddling. "Fannie and Freddie are these massive, enormously profitable institutions where whichever political party controls them…if they're still in conservatorship, can influence the outcome of elections," he told CNBC.

In one scenario, he explained, Democrats win the White House, conservatorship is still in place, and Democrats push Fannie and Freddie to lower credit standards in order to expand home ownership and affordability.

"If they're going to move more aggressively into borrowers with lower credit quality, for example, to achieve a political objective, that's going to have an impact on trillions of dollars outstanding mortgage securities," Ackman said. "It's going to have an impact on overall credit spreads."

MBS investors want certainty about how the entities will be run, he noted.

"That only gets resolved in a world in which they exit conservatorship, they become publicly traded companies that are owned by institutional and retail investors," Ackman said. "We set the rules. In conservatorship, the president can do anything."

#2830. Binance breach puts custody at center of crypto infrastructure trade

The $6.3 billion Binance hack could accelerate a shift in how investors value cryptocurrency companies, putting a greater premium on custody providers and the infrastructure needed to securely hold and protect digital assets.

Much of crypto's evolution this year has involved companies moving past their reliance on trading volumes and transaction fees, to focus instead on building the infrastructure connecting digital assets with traditional finance. Last Thursday's breach adds a new dimension, bringing cybersecurity, custody, compliance and balance-sheet resilience into sharper focus.

Importantly, the Binance breach was not an indictment of crypto itself, or a case of leadership-driven fraud, as with FTX in late 2022. Instead, Binance's leadership moved quickly to contain the fallout, protect customers and commit the exchange's own resources to cover losses.

On Tuesday, Binance CEO Richard Teng told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" that the company has replenished 98% of $6.34 billion in affected assets, and that it is still in the process of purchasing outstanding, more illiquid assets.

Management's response, alongside efforts elsewhere in the industry to boost confidence, helped prevent a security breach from escalating into a broader crisis of confidence. For example, Tether, Circle, Ripple and others moved quickly to freeze or restrict access to about $3 billion in stolen assets; Coinbase blocked transfers to compromised wallets and offered Binance direct assistance.

The hack could even help shape the next phase of the crypto infrastructure trade. The new winners may not just be the businesses with the most users, volume or assets under custody, but the ones that can also demonstrate they're able to protect those assets under extreme duress.

"Which company has the resources to invest in cybersecurity and protect customer funds? For a smaller company, it could be much harder because once these crypto companies become infrastructure plays, providing the well for tokenization … they need to have the compliance and control in place so that a similar hacking will not happen or can be minimized," Owen Lau, senior analyst at ClearStreet, told CNBC. "Larger companies have more resources that could give them some advantage."

While institutional investors have increasingly embraced digital assets, broader adoption depends on confidence that those assets can be securely held, accessed and transferred. The Binance breach highlights the importance of that infrastructure, and could increase demand for specialized custodians and platforms with established asset-protection capabilities.

Coinbase has operated a dedicated institutional custody business since 2018. Circle entered the custody business this year, after the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted it approval to operate as a trust bank. In the past few years, Ripple and Kraken have also launched custody businesses.

Still, smaller players compete in the space as well. Small cap crypto exchange stock Gemini Space Station has offered custody services since 2019. BitGo Holdings, founded in 2013, is one of the earliest players in institutional crypto custody and infrastructure, with a reputation for security and serving major institutions.

The shift could also drive consolidation as companies look to buy capabilities, deepen their infrastructure offerings and achieve the scale needed to compete, Lau said.

The more consequential structural shift may be the separation of custody from execution, according to Morgan Stanley.

"Crypto exchanges have historically combined trading, custody, and settlement within vertically integrated platforms, concentrating operational risk. Repeated security breaches could encourage investors to move assets toward independent custody while continuing to trade on CEXs," the firm's analyst Felix Stratmann said in a note Monday," referring to centralized cryptocurrency exchanges.

"This would preserve the role of centralized exchanges as liquidity and execution venues, while potentially benefiting regulated custodians, including banks, as institutional investors place greater emphasis on asset segregation, operational resilience, and investor protection," Stratmann said.

#2823. When the game is on the line, where has Devin Booker gone?

There was an unfortunate trend that began to manifest itself during the back half of last season. When the going gets tough, your best players need to get going. And unfortunately for the Phoenix Suns, that trend involved Devin Booker's struggles to perform in clutch moments.

From February 1 onward, in 11 clutch games in which Booker played, the Suns went 3-8. During those moments, Booker shot 6-of-20 from the field, recorded five assists against eight turnovers, and posted a -34 plus/minus.

That's concerning, especially when you consider that over his previous 10 seasons, which included some pretty horrible Suns teams, Booker owned a -2 +/- in 316 clutch situations. He shot 40% from the field during those moments and maintained a 1.8 assist-to-turnover ratio.

And it wasn't as if Booker had struggled in the clutch throughout the entirety of last season. Through the first 19 games in which he played, the Suns were 11-8 in clutch situations. Booker shot 51.2% from the field, recorded 10 assists against only three turnovers, and posted a +27 plus/minus. But upon returning from an ankle injury on February 7, the nosedive began.

You can make the argument that it's supposed to be tough, that your best player is naturally going to be the focal point of opposing defenses, and therefore his performance will be hindered by the schemes designed to stop him. During that same timeframe, from February 1 onward, Booker ranked dead last in plus/minus among players who attempted at least 20 shots in clutch situations. Jalen Brunson, Luka Doncic, and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander were at the top of the list, with Brunson posting a +41. And there were plenty of other names ahead of Booker, including Jamal Murray, CJ McCollum, Brandon Ingram, and Desmond Bane.

That only adds to the concern about who Devin Booker is and what he represents at this point in his career, particularly within the context of this Suns team. Because you can make excuses all day long about how he's being double-teamed or triple-teamed, but great players make the necessary adjustments that lead to team success. That's why plus/minus, when evaluated over an extended period, carries considerably more value than looking at the number from a single game. The trend we witnessed last season was concerning.

If double teams are being thrown at Devin Booker, why is he turning the ball over so frequently? Does he not see them coming? You know as well as I do that many of those turnovers come from Booker predictably driving into a crowd of defenders and trying to force the issue rather than relying on the finesse that's been a hallmark of his career.

Why do I bring this up? Because on Monday night against the Golden State Warriors, that familiar trend once again manifested itself. Booker's inability to execute in clutch moments ultimately contributed to another Suns loss. Yes, there are multiple variables involved, including other players who failed to perform when it mattered most. But none of those guys are making $57 million a year.

Booker re-entered the game with the Suns leading 106-104 and 4:48 remaining. A minute later, he connected on a nine-foot jumper, accounting for his only two points in clutch time. From there, things unraveled.

With Phoenix trailing 109-108, Booker missed a wide-open 12-foot jumper. On the following possession, he turned the ball over. After Jalen Green committed a turnover on the next trip down the floor, Booker was called for an offensive foul, his sixth and final foul of the game.

His final clutch stat line? In 3.8 minutes, Booker shot 1-of-2 from the field, grabbed one rebound, committed two turnovers, and posted a -7 plus/minus.

It's not the end of the world, but it does raise concerns that Devin Booker is picking up right where he left off last season, when his ability to impose his will on a game appeared to be a fading trait.

You might look at this as a one-game sample, but I see it as a sample of 11 previous clutch-time games. Perhaps that's still not enough to definitively identify a trend, especially when you consider the body of work Booker has put together over what is now his 12th NBA season. But it's the manner in which these struggles recur, time and again, that has become the focal point of frustration for a fan base desperate for success and watching a team that can ill afford to lose.

Booker's game has become predictable, and his execution in these moments has been subpar. And I know that somewhere, somebody is preparing to show me a collection of all the game winners Booker has made throughout his career. I appreciate every one of those moments and what they've meant to us as Suns fans. In the same breath, hitting a game-winner against Oklahoma City last season doesn't equate to a victory last night against Golden State.

Devin Booker has earned the benefit of the doubt throughout his career, but that doesn't mean he's exempt from scrutiny when the results begin telling a different story. The Suns need their best player to be their best player when possessions matter most. That requires better decisions, cleaner execution, and an ability to recognize what opposing defenses are taking away. Booker's past has established what he's capable of. His present is beginning to raise legitimate questions about his ability to consistently deliver it.

#2818. NFL Secret Superstars: 3 under-the-radar AFC standouts in Week 8

Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it's the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they're needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they're playing in a smaller market, and the media isn't appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they're hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it's always possible that a wayward coach hasn't quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team.

Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here.

Here are our AFC Secret Superstars for Week 8 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven't yet, download the new SB Nation app, so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are!

(All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Focus, Sports Info Solutions, and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated).

The Kansas City Chiefs went for a complete overhaul of their run game this past offseason. They brought back offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy to do the job he'd done from 2018 to 2022, they signed Kenneth Walker III to a three-year, $43.05 million contract with $28.7 million guaranteed, and they selected Nebraska running back Emmett Johnson with the 151st overall pick in the fifth round of the 2026 draft.

Of those moves, the Johnson pick made the fewest waves, but if you had studied Johnson's college tape, there might have been a bit of a zing there. In 2025, the 5'10", 202-pound Johnson ran the ball 251 times for 1,450 yards, 12 touchdowns, 68 forced missed tackles, and 36 runs of 10 or more yards.

Johnson did okay at the combine, but not in ways that represented his on-field dynamism, which may be one reason he dropped as far as he did. We're assuming that the Chiefs are quite happy that it worked out the way it did, especially on Sunday against the Denver Broncos. Kansas City lost that game 28-24 despite a last-second drive that ended on the Denver 12-yard line with a Malcolm Roach sack of Patrick Mahomes, but Johnson went off in that game. He grabbed five catches on five targets for 128 yards and a touchdown, and his one rushing attempt for 15 yards saw him break at least five tackles.

"Obviously Kenneth is the guy, but you want to be able to take carries away from him, so we can have him for the full entire season," Mahomes said postgame. "If Emmett can come in and be a change of pace, break tackles and make plays, catch the ball, do all that different type of stuff, defenses can't relax. I thought he did a great job today, and he's done great the entire time he's been here. As the season goes on, we'll continue to utilize him more and more, but at the same time utilizing Kenneth."

So, the run game is all set. The Chiefs desperately need receiver help before the trade deadline, but at least they have the ground attack going for them, which is nice.

Speaking of surprise backs who are showing up all over the place, there's Braelon Allen of the New York Jets. The 6′ 1¼", 235-pound Allen impressed at Wisconsin as a big power back with some wiggle and explosiveness — he had 592 carries for 3,482 yards, 25 touchdowns, 143 forced missed tackles, and 77 runs of 10 or more yards for the Badgers from 2021-2023 — but that still had him lasting until the 134th overall pick in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, which is where the Jets got him.

With Breece Hall as the main man in the Jets' backfield, it took Allen a while to get his share of the carries. He had just 110 rushing attempts combined in the 2024 and 2025 seasons, but with Hall much more of an injury concern this season (he's missed five straight games with a quadriceps injury), Allen has gotten his shot, and he's made the most of it — especially recently. His 21-carry, 147-yard, one-touchdown performance against the Las Vegas Raiders last Sunday in a frustrating 38-33 loss was just the latest in a series of great games.

Allen also has 20 forced missed tackles since Week 5 (only Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions has more with 26), and nobody in the NFL has more runs of 10 or more yards in that timeframe than Allen's 18.

"Guys up front moving people, just being patient and just letting the game come to me," Allen said, when asked postgame about the secret to his recent success. "Not trying to force anything. Just going by my reads and progressing right. Like I said, the guys up front, they make it happen."

So, how did it feel to score on your first six drives and still lose the game?

"The objective every week is to win," Allen said. "When you don't get that done it's hard to—obviously there's positives always, and I love our progress as a team and as an offense. There are takeaways for sure, positive takeaways, but like I said, the goal is to win. When you don't do that it's hard to enjoy."

Perhaps it would have helped if Allen had more than three carries (for 26 yards) in the second half? When your defense is busy blowing a 23-14 halftime lead, and you're allowing Kirk Cousins to look like Patrick Mahomes in the second half, perhaps toting the rock and bleeding the clock are better options. The Jets had a 19:17-10:43 time of possession advantage in the first half, but at the end of the game, the Raiders had marched back to make it about as even as possible — 30:02 to 29:58 in Gang Green's favor.

Maybe the coaching will catch up to Allen's exploits, and the 2-6 Jets can start to get in front of those games. In the meantime, it helps that Braelon Allen has arrived.

In August, Titans edge-rusher Jacob Martin was asked about the ideal mentality of the his new defensive line after he signed a two-year, $9 million contract with $4.5 million guaranteed.

"We go in there and f**k s**t up," Martin said. "And the linebackers clean it up. I am super thankful to be here, thankful for the opportunity. The team is great, guys are great. A lot of young talent in this building, and I am excited to be a part of this organization, excited to grow, excited to build with these guys. The sky is the limit for sure."

Martin obviously said all of that before the Titans traded Jeffery Simmons, the NFL's best interior defensive lineman, to the Chicago Bears last week for a bevy of draft picks. It's less encouraging when your new team is in full-on fire-sale mode, but against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, Martin was bound and determined to make up for Simmons' absence by any means necessary. Martin has been a good player throughout his career in fits and starts. but you don't play for eight teams in nine seasons if you're one of Those Guys.

He was on Sunday, though. Martin had three sacks, five quarterback hits, and two quarterback hurries in Tennessee's 43-36 overtime loss, and while Joe Burrow absolutely went off for 462 passing yards and six total touchdowns (five passing and one rushing), safety Amani Hooker intercepted three of Burrow's passes, and Martin harassed Burrow and left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. ceaselessly. Inside moves, outside the arc, bull-rushes — the Bengals could do nothing to stop him.

It's important for the rest of the Titans' defensive line to follow suit and "f**k s**t up" as Martin noted. Certainly, with seven sacks and 29 pressures this season, he's doing his part.

The Toronto Raptors completed a double-digit comeback to defeat the Los Angeles Clippers 125-118 at the Intuit Dome.

Toronto, which did not take its first lead until the final two minutes, came through with a clutch fourth-quarter rally to secure the win.

The Raptors found themselves in a similar position against the Lakers the previous night, but their comeback attempt fell short. This time, however, Toronto learned from that experience and finished the job with a hard-fought victory.

The Raptors continued to experiment with their options at centre, giving Trayce Jackson-Davis an opportunity last night before turning to Collin Murray-Boyles tonight, as Jakob Poeltl did not play.

Both teams traded possessions early, with neither side looking particularly sharp offensively. Trading baskets remained the theme for much of the opening quarter, as both teams struggled to find a consistent rhythm.

However, the Clippers began to create some separation behind their three-point shooting. Kobe Sanders led the charge late in the frame, scoring 11 points on 4-of-6 shooting, including 3-of-4 from beyond the arc as the Raptors had no answer for him.

Los Angeles closed the quarter on a 17-5 run, extending its lead to as many as 13 points before heading into the second quarter with an 11-point advantage.

Toronto looked sloppy down the stretch and simply didn't do enough to start the game.

The Raptors showed some signs of life to start the second quarter, with Immanuel Quickley getting Toronto on the board before Scottie Barnes added his first basket of the night. Barnes, who entered the game questionable, had been relatively quiet through the opening stretch.

RJ Barrett also provided a spark offensively, knocking down a three-pointer before scoring on a post-up jumper against former teammate Gradey Dick to bring his total to 16 points.

Toronto's three-point shooting and defensive effort improved, but the Clippers continued to respond whenever the Raptors threatened to build momentum.

Brook Lopez continued to give Toronto problems, taking advantage of the Raptors' smaller lineup on both ends of the floor.

Turnovers also became a major issue for Toronto, with seven giveaways leading to nine Clippers points. Dick continued to put together a strong performance as Los Angeles extended its lead to as many as 15 points.

Toronto also had to manage much of the quarter without Barrett, who picked up his third personal foul. The Raptors had plenty of work to do after heading into halftime trailing 63-52.

INGLEWOOD, CA – NOVEMBER 2: RJ Barrett #9 of the Toronto Raptors looks to pass the ball as Max Strus #31 of the LA Clippers plays defense during the game on November 2, 2026 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, California. Toronto came out of the halftime break with much better energy, as Barnes, Walter and Murray-Boyles helped spark a 6-0 run to cut the Clippers' lead to five. The strong start forced Los Angeles to call an early timeout, but the Clippers quickly settled back into the game and restored their nine-point advantage.

Dick and Sanders continued to build on their impressive nights, with Dick making an impact across the floor and Sanders knocking down a three-pointer to cap an 11-3 Clippers run.

Toronto continued to struggle offensively, with Barrett providing a strong performance but receiving very little help from the rest of the lineup.

Jamison Battle provided a much-needed spark off the bench, knocking down back-to-back three-pointers to bring his total to 12 points. Battle was particularly effective from beyond the arc, shooting 4-of-5 from three-point range.

Although Toronto showed some improvement towards the end of the quarter, the Clippers maintained control and carried a 13-point lead into the fourth. The Raptors needed a strong final quarter, similar to last night if they wanted to make a comeback.

Toronto opened the fourth quarter with back-to-back baskets from Alijah Martin and Scottie Barnes, who quietly recorded a double-double. Barnes and RJ Barrett began to find a rhythm together offensively, helping Toronto chip away at the deficit, while Immanuel Quickley added a pull-up three-pointer to cut the lead to eight.

However, foul trouble continued to be an issue for the Raptors, with Ja'Kobe Walter picking up his fifth personal foul and Barrett his fourth, allowing the Clippers to extend their advantage back to 12.

Los Angeles also lost Brook Lopez to fouls, as he fouled out with five minutes remaining, giving Toronto a potential opening to make a push.

With both teams showing signs of fatigue, Toronto continued to battle and took advantage of opportunities at the free-throw line to work its way back into the game.

Barnes, Quickley and Barrett had carried much of the offensive load throughout the night, and they delivered when it mattered most. Barrett converted a tough layup with under three minutes remaining to tie the game at 109, capping a remarkable 16-4 Raptors run.

Barnes followed with a difficult turnaround fadeaway to give Toronto its first lead of the night. Some clutch free throws from Barnes, Murray-Boyles and Quickley, combined with vintage defensive intensity down the stretch, helped the Raptors complete the fourth-quarter comeback and escape Los Angeles with a hard-fought victory.

Although it was far from a perfect performance, the Raptors showed resilience and refused to give up, earning a crucial victory.

Barnes, Quickley and Barrett led the way for Toronto with strong performances. However, there is still room for improvement, particularly with their three-point shooting, free-throw efficiency and ability to get off to a stronger start.

Raptors fans were hoping to see Kawhi Leonard face his former team, but neither Leonard nor Brandon Ingram suited up. Dick, however, delivered a solid performance against his former team, while Sanders led the Clippers with 26 points. Despite his efforts, Los Angeles could not hold on to its lead and fell to 1-6 on the season.

The Raptors, now 4-3, will enjoy a well-deserved day off tomorrow before travelling to Denver to take on the Nuggets on Wednesday. Tip-off is scheduled for 9 p.m.

#2808. Kyler Murray's hamstring issue could be cover for a soft benching

How can the Vikings bench Kyler Murray without benching Kyler Murray?

They can rely on an injury through which he otherwise would be able to play.

It’s hard not to look at the current status of Murray’s hamstring “tightness” as cover for a soft benching of Murray. That gives the Vikings a chance to let Carson Wentz, who played well enough in most of the Week 1 win over the Packers and all of the Week 2 win over the Bears.

While the Vikings will never admit to that strategy, consider this undeniable fact: On Tuesday, offensive coordinator Wes Phillips was asked for an assessment of Murray’s play “in the past couple weeks.”

“I don’t really want to get into, like, overarching, ‘Hey, this is this is the . . .,” Phillips said. “You know, the fact of the matter is, you know, we lost the game against a tough [Lions] football team on the road. It’s a division game. It stings, but we’ve got to get better moving forward.  And, you know, we’ll see as the week goes on, where we’re at in that spot . . . but, yeah, we’ve got to get better. We’re going to actively pursue every avenue we can to make that happen.”

This implies, if taken literally, pursuing every avenue toward acquiring an upgrade via a trade — whether that’s Jacoby Brissett, Daniel Jones, Kirk Cousins, or even Justin Herbert.

It all comes down to whether the Vikings are content to keep doing what they’ve been doing, or whether they’ll make a move aimed at significantly upgrading a position that, in recent weeks, has not been good enough.

Yes, they’re 6-1. That’s better than anyone could have expected them to be. But it’s not because Murray has turned the clock back to the early years of his career. His passer rating (86.6) is toward the bottom of all qualifying quarterbacks (and, in fairness, that’s higher than the numbers generated by Brissett, Jones, and Herbert).

It’s the lowest number for any season of Murray’s career, and the overall performance is less than what the Vikings need to maximize their current formula.

Especially since he’s not getting the ball to receiver Justin Jefferson. That’s something Wentz did consistently in 2025, making Wentz the preferred option to J.J. McCarthy — who returned to the lineup following a Week 2 ankle injury only after Wentz suffered a season-ending shoulder injury in Week 8.

If McCarthy was still in Minnesota, there would be an unavoidable groundswell to give him a shot. But he lost the No. 2 job to Wentz. Which means Wentz won it.

Which means that the Vikings could be thinking about giving Wentz a Monday night audition against the Bills, with a plan to make a possible trade the next day if things don’t go well.

For now, the rest of the week will reveal whether and to what extent Murray or Wentz will take the first-team reps at practice. And whether Murray or Wentz will play on Monday night.

It won’t be a surprise if it’s Wentz against the Bills. Even if Murray is technically healthy enough to play.

#2801. Owono ‘deeply affected’ by De Miguel’s death, says Andorra team-mate

Jesus Owono's team-mate has insisted the Andorra goalkeeper would never intend to hurt a fellow player following the death of Jesus de Miguel.

The Tenerife forward died on Tuesday morning following a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

Owono was sent off for the clash having raced from his goal and struck 30-year-old De Miguel at force, with the Tenerife player subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest.

There has been shock and grief across football following the tragic incident, while Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter.

That is, though, standard practice under Spanish law and Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui told Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings were "very unlikely".

Andorra's Argentinian defender Lautaro Spatz took to Instagram to pay tribute to De Miguel but also to defend Owono, who has deleted his account on the social media platform.

Spatz called De Miguel's death "a tragedy that has left us completely broken, without words and with a sadness difficult to explain".

The 25-year-old continued: "I also want to have some words for my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened.

"Those of us who know him know the type of person he is, how much he is suffering in these moments and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

"In football, unfortunate incidents happen but no-one could imagine that one of these could end in such tragic circumstances."

Fans gathered at Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium to lay tributes to De Miguel, with the club declaring six days of official mourning.

A memorial service will be held at the ground on Saturday evening for the striker, with supporters invited to attend.

Tuesday's domestic Spanish games were called off as a mark of respect but Champions League matches went ahead, including Barcelona's clash with Aston Villa at the Nou Camp.

A minute's silence was held ahead of the contest, which Barça won 3-0, with Raphinha scoring twice.

Speaking to CBS Sports afterwards, the Brazilian refused to talk about the game, saying: "I want to send a lot of strength to the family of Jesus. Today I'm not going to talk about football.

"For me, the truth is it was quite difficult (to play). After seeing the news, of course I didn't have good feelings. He's a fellow player and it could have happened to anyone, it could have happened to me.

"He was the same age as me, I don't know if that's why it affected me more. It's been a difficult day. Personally, it touched me a lot."

The Tenerife match was suspended after the incident, which occurred in stoppage time, with distressed players calling for immediate medical attention.

A statement from Tenerife announcing De Miguel's death read: "We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones… that today weep for this cruel outcome."

In their own statement on Tuesday evening, Andorra said the club were "deeply shocked", adding: "The first thing we want to do is express our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife and all those who were close to him.

"We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we are by their side and that we deeply share their sadness."

#2800. NFL’s Secret Superstars, Week 8: 3 under-the-radar standouts from the NFC

Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it's the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they're needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they're playing in a smaller market, and the media isn't appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they're hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it's always possible that a wayward coach hasn't quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team.

Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here.

Here are our NFC Secret Superstars for Week 8 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven't yet, download the new SB Nation app, so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are!

(All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Focus, Sports Info Solutions, and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated).

Baseball delineates its pitchers very specifically between starters and relievers. There are times when I think that NFL teams should do the same thing. If your quarterback is struggling to start a game, why should he automatically be able to finish it without question? Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur ran into this situation when his team went up against the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday. Starter Jacoby Brissett completed just 10 of 23 passes for 119 yards, no touchdowns, one interception, four sacks, and a passer rating of 41.8. When that's all you can do against a Dallas defense that should apologize for even taking the field every week, it's time to sub your starter out.

Which is what LaFleur did. Backup Gardner Minshew took his first snap of the day with 1:35 left in the third quarter with the Cardinals down 17-3, and things were never the same from there. Minshew tore through that alleged defense as it should be, completing 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 137.3. Everything Brissett struggled with, Minshew had on the ball right away, and that's how the Cardinals erased a major deficit to win the game in overtime, 33-30.

"Yeah, he did a good job," LaFleur said of Minshew after the win. "Obviously, extended a few plays, stuff like that, but I thought his timing was great. I mean, he's had a lot of success in this league, guys, and he's about as resilient as they come, too. If you ask Gardner Minshew, I mean, he's ready at all times. And I thought the guys made some plays for him, and he was getting the ball out of his hands. Obviously, kind of what unlocked it to start was — it starts with a six-yard completion to [receiver Devin] Duvernay, and then we obviously have that long run by TA [running back Tyler Allgeier] to unlock and loosened them up. That's why you need explosives and big plays, because it loosens people up."

Apparently, Minshew did enough to loosen everybody up, because it was reported on Monday that he'll be the starter going forward. That can be a bumpy ride, as Minshew has proven throughout his career, but LaFleur had no choice. When the Cowboys' defense has you on pause, it's time to make a change.

"I think [Minshew] kind of showed all of us in terms of him going out there being the competitor that he is," LaFleur said on Monday after the decision was made. "Doesn't shock me. The production was pretty wild in terms of the amount of points and just moving up and down the field, but he's a competitor and he's always prepared. He's preparing like he's the starter. He's preparing like he's going to be in there for whatever snap. He supported Jacoby at a high level too. He's been a great backup for him. He's been great for the room and [I] look forward to the challenge that we have this week with him."

Nobody had any right to expect what the Tampa Bay Buccaneers did to the Atlanta Falcons last Sunday. Coming into Week 8, Jeff Ulbrich's Falcons defense was tied for third in the NFL in opponent EPA per rush at -.016, tied with the Seattle Seahawks, behind only the Jacksonville Jaguars (-0.21) and the San Francisco 49ers (-0.18).

So, how on Earth did the Bucs run 56 times for 324 yards against that estimable defense? Especially with Baker Mayfield failing to complete a single pass? The game was played in monsoon-like conditions, but it started with backs Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell. In the Bucs' 16-0 win, Irving ran 27 times for 170 yards, a touchdown, seven forced missed tackles, and five runs of 10 or more yards. Gainwell ran 25 times for 140 yards, nine forced missed tackles, and five runs of 10 or more yards.

It was an ass-kicking from start to finish.

The numbers, per NFL Research and Next Gen Stats, were astonishing.

The Buccaneers became the first team in 52 seasons (Buffalo on Sept. 29, 1974) to win a game with no pass completions and the first team in 20 years (Houston on Dec. 3, 2006) to win a game with zero-or-fewer net passing yards.

Irving and Gainwell became the first pair of teammates in 50 seasons and the fourth pair of teammates in NFL history each with at least 20 rushing attempts and 125 rushing yards in the same game, joining San Francisco's Wilbur Jackson and Delvin Williams (Nov. 29, 1976), Cleveland's Pro Football Hall of Fame duo of Jim Brown and Bobby Mitchell (Dec. 13, 1959), and the Los Angeles Rams' Ron Waller and Tank Younger (Dec. 4, 1955).

Per Next Gen Stats, the Buccaneers called a designed run on 90.0% of plays against the Falcons, the highest rate in a single game since 2021 and the 2nd-highest rate in a game in the NGS era.

"I thought we did a good job until the fourth quarter," Falcons safety Jessie Bates said of his team's run-stopping efforts. "The first three quarters I really thought we contained, and I think that fourth quarter it really got out of hand. That's what happens. You have to bring your hard hat and be able to stop the run, and we didn't do that. Their defense did a good job of stopping our run, so that's what it comes down to at the end of the day."

Well, that's not quite true — Tampa Bay's rushing yards were pretty evenly distributed by quarter (68, 83, 98, and 80 yards), though the Bucs ran the ball 19 times in the final 15 minutes. Overall, they threw just about every run concept at Atlanta's defense — at least 16.1% inside zone, outside zone, man, and counter — and Atlanta, quite unusually, had no answers.

Bates had all kinds of good things to say about Irving, who has run the ball 147 times this season for 748 yards, five touchdowns, 31 forced missed tackles, and 16 runs of 10 or more yards.

"He's not your traditional back. He is almost similar to our No. 7 [Bijan Robinson] over here – you think the play is over. They run these duo runs that are supposed to hit downhill, and you've gotta cover every single gap with No. 7 [Irving]. Like I said, I thought we did a good job containing them up until a couple big runs that he had. Much respect to those guys, and we will see them again."

The rematch happens in Week 16 on Sunday, December 27. We'll see if the Buccaneers will have re-installed their passing game by then, or if they want to just go ground-and-pound until somebody (anybody) can stop them.

The Green Bay Packers have risen from 19th in Defensive DVOA in the 2025 season to fourth through Week 8 in 2026 under new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, who replaced Jeff Hafley when Hafley became the Miami Dolphins' head coach. And they've done that with missing pieces on the roster. Micah Parsons has been out the entire season so far with the torn ACL he suffered last December, and linebackers Edgerrin Cooper (season-ending ruptured Achilles tendon) and Zaire Franklin (hairline shin fracture) have also been missed.

The good news for the Packers Gannon is how well the "replacements" have stepped in. And among those understudies, it's tough to imagine anybody doing better than linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper, the 2024 third-round pick from Missouri by way of Florida, who has seen his snap counts and importance to Gannon's defense spike up considerably of late.

Hopper had just 151 total snaps in 2024 and 2025 combined; he's already exceeded that by 60 this season. And he was never better than in Green Bay's 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers last Thursday night. In that game, Hopper totaled one sack, four pressures, six solo tackles, three pass breakups, and an interception.

With that, Hopper became the first Packers player since Hall of Famer Charles Woodson in 2009 to record three pass breakups, a sack, and an interception in the same game.

"Ty'Ron Hopper. I can't say enough great things about him," Matt LaFleur said postgame. "The night he had. I think, what? Sack, PBU, interception? What a great performance. I think that's something that we did see coming more so in the pre season. I can't say enough about the job that obviously [linebackers coach] Sam Siefkes does with our inside linebackers to get them ready, and I just see a lot of growth from that group. They're playing really well."

The Packers' defense has been great already, and with Micah Parsons estimated to be back to practicing this week? It might be a whole lot better. In the meantime, guys like Hopper and recent Secret Superstar Evan Williams have been holding it down with authority.

"I mean, you hold a team to 103 points in the NBA, you should be able to win a lot of games," Fernández said.

Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle (30) drives to the basket against New York Knicks center Andre Drummond (0) on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026, in New York. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

This season, the Nets received a much-needed infusion of talent — two-time All-NBA selection Julius Randle and No. 6 overall pick Mikel Brown Jr., along with Mo Wagner and Keon Ellis — but the team has struggled to develop offensive chemistry.

Through seven games, the Nets (1-6) rank 29th in scoring (105.6), 28th in offensive rating, 29th in assist to turnover ratio (1.21), 28th in turnover percentage (18.3) and 28th in field goal percentage (41.7).

"I think it's more about us not being organized, and then if you have empty possessions, you don't run anything for anybody, like nobody's in the right spot," Fernández said. "You don't touch the paint. You don't move. You don't reverse the ball, and you get either no shots or terrible shots. … Everybody's got to do their jobs because whether we call a play or not, you got to run to your spots, and we didn't do it enough times, and that's the frustrating thing. When we do it, we get good results. When we don't do it, we get bad results.

Brooklyn Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez watches his team during the first half of an NBA basketball game against the New York Knicks, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. AP Photo/Frank Franklin II

Randle is averaging a career-high 4.1 turnovers per game and shooting 41.5 percent from the field, well down from his career mark (47.2). #2789. Bo Nix has 15 game-winning drives, most ever for a QB in his first three seasons

The Broncos trailed the Chiefs 24-13 with 10 minutes left on Sunday, but anyone who thought the Broncos were out of it hasn’t been watching Bo Nix.

Nix led Denver’s offense to two touchdowns and a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter of a 28-24 win, marking Nix’s 15th career game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime. No quarterback in NFL history has as many game-winning drives in his first three seasons as Nix.

Dak Prescott, who had 14 game-winning drives in his first three seasons, had the previous record. Nix has surpassed Prescott and isn’t even halfway through his third season.

A game-winning drive is defined as an offensive scoring drive in the fourth quarter or overtime that puts a team ahead for the final time. Nix had three of them as a rookie in 2024, an NFL-high seven of them last year, and has an NFL-high five of them already this year.

The all-time leader in game-winning drives is Tom Brady, who had 58 of them. It would take Nix many years to catch Brady, but being more than a quarter of the way there through two and a half seasons is an impressive achievement.

#2788. Statistical dive into Denver Broncos record-tying 15th straight win in one-score games

The Denver Broncos have now won 15 straight regular season games that were decided by one-score (8 or fewer points). This ties the 2007-2008 Peyton Manning-led Colts. Since the start of the 2025 season the Broncos are 16 and 2 in one-score games in the regular season (1-1 in the post-season). This is a big change from 2024 when the Broncos were 1-6 in one-score games.

The positive change for the Broncos in being able to win one-score games has coincided with Chiefs forgetting how to win one-score games. They were 11-0 in one-score games in 2024 and they have gone 3-10 since.

As good as the Broncos have been in one-score games since the start of the 2025 regular season, the 49ers have had the same winning percentage, 0.889, just in half the games. They are 8-1. The two worst teams are the Chiefs and the Titans. Both have a 0.231 win percentage. Both in 13 games (3-10).

Many of these one-score games have involved Bo Nix leading a fourth quarter comeback (4QC) and a game-winning drive (GWD). Both can only occur in the 4th quarter or overtime and can only happen in a win. If the QB leads a drive to take the lead and then the defense allows a GWD by the opposing QB, the Bronco QB does not get either.

Bo Nix has now started 42 NFL games and has lead 12 4QC and 15 GWD. Those are the highest values for any QB at this point in his career in NFL history.

The only QBs who are close is in 4QC are Tom Brady and Justin Herbert. Both have 10 in the first 3 starting seasons. Dak Prescott is the only one who is close in GWD. He had 14 in his first 48 starts (first 3 seasons). Tom Brady is the career leaded in 4QC with 46. He did that in 333 career starts. Bo has 12 in 42. Brady had one every 7.24 starts in his career. Bo has one every 3.50 starts. Brady also has the most GWD in his career with 58. He had one GWD every 5.74 starts. Nix has one every 2.80 starts. Bo's numbers are best in history (min 32 GS) for both 4QC and GWD.

Now some context, it takes a special set of circumstances to get either a 4QC or a GWD. There is some luck involved. The 3 and out drive for the FG after the interception in OT against the Seahawks gained 8 yards. But Bo Nix still got a GWD for that drive. That was luck and good, good defense. So a QB needs to be playing for a team with a good defense to get either. Tom Brady had this early in his career as Belicheat almost always had good to great defenses.

QBs also need to be on a team with decent offense: good enough to keep the game at least close, but not good enough to win in blow-outs. By the same token, if the defense is inconsistent, the QB might be on the wrong side of blow-out losses.

If the Bronco offense ever figures things out (they had four 3-and-outs last game), the opportunities for these two stats should go away because the Broncos will be playing with leads. That is what the Bronco defense is designed to be at its best – rushing the passer and defending against the pass with a lead. That didn't work too well at the end of the last game, but when both starting safeties are out, it changes things.

For historical context, as a rookie Nix had 3 4QC and 3 GWD. Last season he had 5 and 7. He already has 4 and 5 this season. However, the 5 GWD is not the most in the NFL. Somehow PFR is showing the Browns with 6 GWD when they only have 5 wins. That makes no sense until you realize that they credited two different QBs with a GWD (Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson) for the same game. I have never seen that before.

The Broncos are currently 22nd in scoring at 21.5 ppg with a full 8 weeks of the season completed. The rushing offense is tied for 25th at 3.78 yards per carry (tied with Dallas). Although part of that is a result of just how ineffective JK Dobbins has been so far this season as a runner. His 3.26 yards per touch is tied for 3rd worst among RBs with 35 or more carries. Only Kendre Miller and Dameon Pierce have been worse this season. Contrast that with RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman who (aided by long catches) are near the top of the league in yards per touch for RBs.

The Broncos converted 2 of 11 third downs against the Chiefs and now sit at dead last in the NFL on 3rd down conversion rate at 29.7 percent. The Commanders are second worst at 31.9%. The Bengals have been the best so far this season at 52.9 percent. The 49ers at 50.0 percent exactly are second. Thankfully the Broncos have been able to convert on 5 of 6 4th downs, but 3rd down efficiency needs to improve or this team won't make the playoffs.

Jeremy Crawshaw is 4th in net yards per punt and he is tied for the league lead in punts downed inside the 10 at 10 (tied with Michael Dickson). He is also leading the league in "Inside the 10" points (trademarked) with 45. See below. For this a punter gets one point for a punt downed at 10, 2 for one downed at the 9, etc. While Crawshaw has yet to get one downed at the one or two this season, he has 10 of his 41 punts downed at or inside the 10. 41 punts is tied for most in the league (with the Eagles' punter).

The sack total for the defense sits at 23 after 8 games. They are 3 behind the league leading Steelers, but Kermit has always been hard to sack, so getting him twice last game is admirable. The Lions and Vikings are also ahead of the Broncos with 24 and 25 and they both have only played 7 games. The Bronco defense is looking to become the first team in NFL history to lead the NFL in sacks for three straight seasons.

#2787. Kawhi Leonard injury update: Raptors star finishes knee treatment but still out

Kawhi Leonard is headed back to Toronto. Getting back on the court is the next step.

The Raptors announced Tuesday, Nov. 3 that Leonard, 35, has completed treatment for swelling in his left knee and will begin the return-to-play process in Toronto. The team will update his progress in one week.

Leonard has missed five consecutive games. He felt something in the knee during pregame warmups Oct. 25 and was scratched from a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. An MRI showed no structural damage.

Coach Darko Rajakovic said Oct. 29 that Leonard was getting his treatment outside of Toronto. At the time, NBA insider Chris Haynes reported Leonard would miss at least three to four weeks. The Raptors didn't say Tuesday whether that window has changed.

Leonard already has injury history with the right knee. Leonard tore the ACL in his right knee in the 2021 NBA playoffs and the meniscus in the 2023 playoffs – both with the Los Angeles Clippers.

Toronto brought the two-time NBA Finals MVP back this offseason, sending Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks to Los Angeles. The deal was agreed to in late June, then sat until September while the NBA investigated the Clippers and Leonard for a salary cap circumvention scheme. The league fined Leonard $700,000. He signed a two-year, $115 million extension with Toronto soon after.

Leonard played in the Raptors' first two games, both wins. He averaged 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals but shot just 32.4% from the field. Last season, he played 65 games for the Clippers and averaged 27.9 points.

The Raptors (4-3) are 2-3 without him. The next update is due Nov. 10.

#2783. Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Packers ahead of Week 9

New England Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf knows the Green Bay Packers well. And now, the same goes for offensive quality control coach T.C. McCartney, defensive quality control coach Jamael Lett, outside linebackers coach DeMarcus Covington and special teams coordinator Cam Achord.

But there's also those in the locker rooms. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, seven players currently in the fold have been members of both clubs during the NFL careers.

Here's a glance through the ex-Patriots and ex-Packers ahead of Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium.

Pierre Strong Jr., running back — Selected by Bill Belichick's war room in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL draft at No. 127 overall, Strong checked into 15 games as a rookie. The FCS All-American out of South Dakota State handled 100 rushing yards, 42 receiving yards, 115 kickoff return yards and his first NFL touchdown across 23 all-purpose opportunities that season. He was traded to the Cleveland Browns at the cutdown deadline the following August in exchange for offensive tackle Tyrone Wheatley Jr. After two campaigns in the AFC North, Strong spent 2025 on the practice squad of the Packers and now resides on Green Bay's 53-man roster. The 27-year-old running back stands 50 games into his career and with 116 carries for 536 yards, 34 catches for 243 yards, 24 kickoff returns for 570 yards and a pair of touchdowns.

Jonnu Smith, tight end — Smith totaled 55 receptions for 539 yards and one touchdown across 30 games with the Patriots. The 31-year-old's stay spanned 19 starts and reached its end halfway through a four-year contract. A trade with the Atlanta Falcons during the 2023 offseason brought a seventh-rounder back in return. And on the heels of being named to the Pro Bowl while a member of the Miami Dolphins in 2024, Smith was dealt to the Pittsburgh Steelers. A one-year deal then got him to Lambeau Field in August. Originally entering the NFL with the Tennessee Titans at pick No. 100 overall in the 2017 draft, the Florida International product has amassed 351 catches, 28 carries, 3,819 yards and 32 touchdowns from scrimmage across 148 career games. Mike Mularkey and Mike Vrabel served as the tight end's head coaches in the AFC South before he agreed to terms at Gillette Stadium.

David Blay Jr., defensive tackle — The Packers added Blay to the practice squad at the end of September. The 23-year-old defensive tackle originally entered the NFL in Foxborough as part of the organization's undrafted class of 2026. He was waived by the Patriots two weeks into training camp and finished his rookie preseason with the Philadelphia Eagles before going through the wire unclaimed and catching on in Wisconsin. Blay made collegiate stops at West Chester, Louisiana Tech and Miami while appearing in 46 games.

John Saunders Jr., safety — Saunders joined Green Bay's practice squad on Tuesday after making autumn stops on scout teams in Ohio and New Jersey. The 25-year-old intercepted a pass in August preseason action with New England before being let go at the 53-man roster deadline. Last fall, as an undrafted rookie by way of Miami of Ohio and Ole Miss, Saunders had been added to the Patriots' active roster off the practice squad of the Dolphins. He agreed to remain in the fold as a member of the practice squad for the rest of 2025 after clearing waivers.

Romeo Doubs, wide receiver — The Patriots placed Doubs on injured reserve six games into the fall after he suffered a shoulder injury on a 42-yard touchdown catch. Signed to a four-year deal as an unrestricted free agent in March, the veteran wide receiver stands with 14 receptions for 261 yards and three visits to the end zone this campaign in Foxborough. Not eligible for a return until late November, Doubs originally entered the NFL with Green Bay in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at No. 132 overall. The 26-year-old Nevada product started 50 of his 59 games as a Packer while reeling in 216 passes for 2,424 yards and 21 touchdowns.

Greg Van Roten, guard — Van Roten landed on injured reserve in late September with a thigh injury. It was sustained at right guard during the 106th start and 147th game of his NFL journey. The 36-year-old had visited amid training camp and soon circled back on a one-year pact. First setting out as an undrafted rookie with the Green Bay Packers in 2012, the former All-Ivy League honoree out of Penn appeared in 10 games across two seasons there. Van Roten has been a member of eight different NFL organizations as well as the CFL's Toronto Argonauts since then. He logged back-to-back ironman campaigns with the New York Giants before taking on a depth role at Gillette Stadium.

Mike Brown, safety — Brown earned a promotion to New England's 53-man roster in October after twice serving as a standard elevation from the practice squad. The 27-year-old safety first landed with the Patriots after not being tendered as a restricted free agent in March. Through six games, he has handed nine tackles while seeing 38 snaps on defense and 127 snaps on special teams. Entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2022, the Miami of Ohio alum spent his first preseason with the Minnesota Vikings and had a stint on Green Bay's practice squad before returning to his previous NFC North club. After moving on to Cleveland later in his rookie campaign and appearing in three games, he was signed to head coach Mike Vrabel's former Titans 53-man roster. The Tennessee tenure featured 59 tackles and a handful of starts across 35 contests.

#2778. Bills trade deadline candidate: Colts receiver Josh Downs

Let's jump back to wide receiver for the Buffalo Bills ahead of this year's NFL trade deadline, which is now less than a week away.

Highlighted today is Colts wideout Josh Downs, a fourth-year, nifty slot receiver veteran with 228 career catches and 12 touchdown grabs across three-plus seasons who resides on an Indianapolis team that sits at 2-6, has already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and many believe remains in fire sale mode.

This article is the ninth in the trade-candidate series I'll continue to sprinkle onto the site until the actual trade deadline until November 10.

Derwin James, Brian Thomas Jr. Jessie Bates, Tariq Woolen, Amani Hooker, Antoine Winfield Jr., Cam Bynum, Zack Baun

Selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft after an illustrious career at the University of North Carolina catching passes from Drake Maye, Downs been one of the steadiest slot wideouts in football with high-caliber separation talent.

As a rookie, he caught 68 passes for 771 yards with two scores, and 30 of those 68 snags went for first downs despite a seriously low aDOT of 7.4.

Downs saw nine more targets in 2023 — up from 98 to 107 — and provided an uptick in production with 72 grabs for 803 yards with five receiving scores. Last year, Downs was only targeted 84 times and caught 58 passes for 566 yards and four touchdowns.

Entering Week 9, he averages 4.1 yards and just under 45 receptions per game.

Despite his 5'9", 171-pound frame suggesting he'd need to live in the slot to succeed in the NFL, Downs has proven capable of making plays on the outside, and much of that is thanks to his incredibly shiftiness to beat press coverage from longer corners on the outside. His highest regular-season slot rate was 84.5% in 2024.

While Downs' aDOT has hovered without much variance, between 6.7 yards to 8.4 yards in his first three seasons, he carries a noticeably higher aDOT of 10.3 into Week 9. That's still pretty low overall, but it's in the neighborhood of CeeDee Lamb's (10.6) and the aDOT of Ja'Marr Chase (10.7) and Justin Jefferson (also 10.7) currently.

Also, entering this season, Downs averaged three drops per season and currently has a very solid career contested-catch win rate of 44.9%. Darn good figures for a small receiver.

Downs would be a fascinating fit in Buffalo, because he's not the exact type of vertical threat the team seemingly needs. However, he's a ridiculous separator… and there's no doubt the Bills could use more weapons who can uncover quickly.

Downs is third in the NFL among all receivers who've run at least 100 routes in Fantasy Points Data's Average Separation Score. It's a metric that stems from play-by-play charting of whether or not a wideout got open on a route.

He's been in the Top 30 of Average Separation Score in each of the past two seasons and has ascended to elite-level status in 2026.

But make no mistake about it, this is a possession, mostly underneath receiver who'd amplify the Bills' ability to feature a control-the-clock, quick-strike passing offense when needed.

If the Bills trade for Downs after Week 9, they'd be on the hook for $1.96M in prorated 2026 base salary. Buffalo — with its roughly $4M in 2026 space currently —could slide him right onto their books without any accounting gymnastics.

Given this is Year 4 for Downs in the NFL, and he wasn't a first round pick, his rookie deal is set to expire after the season.

Using Syndicate32.com's trade machine, adding the "fire sale" component to the assessment, the projected cost to trade for Downs is a mid third-round pick in 2027.

While that may seem a touch high for Downs, he has established himself as someone very good in his niche role, and he's very cheap this season.

I don't know if I'd send a third-round pick to Indianapolis for Downs on the first ask. A fourth-rounder, and we're cooking.

What I'd love about this addition is simple — he gets open. Regularly. That's most vital in today's NFL at the receiver position.

Downs is a valuable asset to have in blitzing situations because of how quickly he gets open too.

While he's averaging a higher aDOT than ever, Downs would not solve Buffalo's slight issue with pushing the football downfield.

And would their be a little redundancy with Downs and Khalil Shakir? Sure. But we shouldn't assume skill-set redundancy in the receiver room is a negative. Heck, the Bills have had plenty of larger, rebounder types with separation issues over the past few seasons… why not add another nimble, slot-based wideout who gets open on a regular basis?

Don't forget, when Allen ascended to superstardom, the Bills had Stefon Diggs, John Brown, and Cole Beasley… who brought slightly different specialities to the field but all had skill sets that allowed them to consistently separate.

The kicker on Downs — this trade would keep him away from reuniting with his college quarterback in New England.

But don't get me wrong, the main reason I'd love Downs in Buffalo — he's cheap now, entering his prime… and the dude routinely gets open.

#2777. Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz expresses support for former Hawkeyes LB Jack Campbell

Anyone who follows football and who cares about the men who play the game remains deeply concerned about the health and well-being of Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who remains hospitalized after suffering a neck injury during Sunday’s game against the Vikings.

His coach at Iowa, Kirk Ferentz, opened a Tuesday press conference by addressing Campbell’s current situation.

“I want to share our support, certainly to the family, and most importantly to Jack,” Ferentz said. “And I’ve been in contact with the family, expressed that to them, and they’ve kept us updated, but we’re gonna respect their wishes right now. They’ll handle the information that comes out. When they think it’s appropriate, they’ll release that information and go from there.

“And just, you know, real briefly, I think all of you know, just how impactful Jack was in our program, what a tremendous person he is, what a tremendous player he’s been for us, and then now he’s moved on and done the same exact thing in Detroit, not only playing really well, but just a tremendous leader and tremendous addition. So we’re all keeping him in our thoughts, and certainly, you know, hope everybody that’s a Hawkeye fan does the same.”

Campbell played for Iowa from 2019 through 2022, before becoming a first-round pick of the Lions in 2023. In 2022, he was a first-team All-American, the Big Ten defensive player of the year, and the winner of the Butkus Award as the nation’s top linebacker.

#2776. NBA rescinds Luka Dončić's technical foul during win over Heat, bringing him back to 1 on the season

Luka Dončić's latest technical foul has been called off.

The league rescinded a technical foul the Los Angeles Lakers star picked up during LA's 138-117 win over the Miami Heat on Monday night. The foul, which Dončić earned in the second quarter at Crypto.com Arena, was reviewed by the league Tuesday.

That has brought Dončić to a single technical foul in eight games this season.

The incident Monday happened after Dončić reacted to a call an official made, which led to a candid conversation between Dončić and the officials on the broadcast.

"I clapped. That's a technical? Come on now," Dončić told the official. "If it was anybody else, you know it's not a technical. Come on now."

Klay Thompson hit the free throw after the technical, which brought the Heat within five points at the time.

Dončić was asked about the technical after the game, but he declined to get into it.

Dončić finished with 42 points, 13 assists and 7 rebounds in the win. He's averaged 43.4 points per game over the last five outings, which included a 52-point night against the Utah Jazz on Oct. 25.

Dončić has had issues with technical fouls. He was suspended for a game last season after reaching the 16-technical foul threshold, which triggers an automatic one-game suspension. He had three straight seasons with 15 technical fouls each, and 13 during the 2024-25 campaign.

Two players in the league already have three technical fouls this season. Golden State star Draymond Green is one of them after he was ejected Monday night for an incident during the Warriors' win over the Phoenix Suns. Houston's Jabari Smith Jr. also has three.

It's still very early in the regular season, and Dončić has a long way to go before having to worry about such a penalty again. But having Monday's rescinded undoubtedly gives him extra room to work with down the stretch.

#2775. Report: Russell Wilson interviews for NC State head-coaching job

Former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson, who’s in his first year as a member of The NFL Today on CBS, is exploring a possible Saturday gig.

Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, Wilson interviewed on Tuesday for the head-coaching vacancy at NC State.

Wilson spent four years at NC State, from 2007 through 2010, before transferring to Wisconsin after the Wolfpack opted to go with Mike Glennon for 2011.

The 10-time Pro Bowler has no coaching experience. The reported favorite for the job, former NFL and NC State quarterback Philip Rivers, has high-school coaching experience only.

If nothing else, the interview puts Wilson on the radar screen for other coaching jobs, at the college and pro level. His potential aspirations to coach were not, before now, widely known.

#2774. How Trevor Heman has become one of Missouri's all-time great high school wide receivers

SPRINGFIELD — Trevor Heman cannot be stopped this season.

Actually, Glendale's star wide receiver hasn't been stopped in his career.

After last week's district win over Rolla, Heman has collected 3,881 career receiving yards. This is the fifth-best receiving mark in Missouri high school football history.

"Coming into high school, I didn't even think about that," Heman said. "I didn't even know if that would be feasible. It's awesome to be up there in the record books."

Heman has also collected 275 career receptions. He ranks No. 3 in Missouri history in career receptions.

New Covenant Academy volleyball: Lexi Burks helps the Warriors chase state title

Heman is a fearless wide receiver. He's made catches down the middle of the field utilizing his speed. He uses his agility to make quick cuts and turn short-yardage receptions into big gains.

Heman has also run across the middle of the field, securing catches while being crushed by opposing defenders. He's a head coach's best friend. He's a player that can always be relied upon in the toughest circumstances.

"He's phenomenal at getting open. He has an incredible catch radius," Glendale head coach Frank Tristan said. "Every time he is targeted, he's catching it."

Heman has increased his catches each season. He caught 48 passes during his freshman season, followed by 52 receptions in his sophomore year. Last season, Heman caught 74 passes and has eclipsed 100 receptions this year.

Heman's been on a tear, scoring 27 career touchdowns. He's alongside fellow wide receiver Joelle Rover, who continues to shine in big-play opportunities, too.

Glendale football: Falcons fend off Rolla's final drive to advance past district quarterfinals

Heman will need a huge game against Helias to move into the No. 4 spot in receiving yards. West Platte's Erick Roe holds the fourth-place spot with 4,057 yards. Glendale's Luke Montgomery is No. 2 with 4,698 yards, trailing only to Hillcrest's Dorial Green-Beckham with 6,356 yards.

In career receptions, Heman is behind Cameron's Eric Anderson with 282 receptions for No. 2. Green-Beckham holds a Missouri record with 297 career receptions from 2008-11.

"I'll always be up there for the rest of my life, hopefully," Heman said with a smile.

Glendale takes on No. 1 Helias on the road in the district semifinals on Friday, Nov. 6.

#2773. Bills reverse course on "high-maintenance" C.J. Gardner-Johnson

The Bills said they’d be keeping safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. And now they’re not.

Tuesday’s surprise move to release the veteran defensive back directly contradicts the comments made publicly by coach Joe Brady, on the same day Gardner-Johnson received a one-game suspension for spitting on an opponent during the Week 6 game against the Raiders.

“Look, C.J.'s a member of the Buffalo Bills,” Brady said on October 19. “We brought him here for a reason, and we know that he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team, and, you know, just like everybody else, right, we’ve got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes.”

As one source explained it to PFT, the Bills decided that Gardner-Johnson was simply too “high-maintenance” — and that the talent and production didn’t justify the headaches.

Plenty of other teams could have told the Bills what would happen. Gardner-Johnson has hopscotched around the league, from the Saints to the Eagles to the Lions to the Eagles (again) to the Texans to the Ravens to the Bears to the Bills.

He has been good enough to get more chances, but not good enough to keep him around in light of the issues that he brings with him.

The Bills hoped to harness his attitude in order to give the defense a lift. In the end, however, the baggage outweighed the boost.

And now Gardner-Johnson becomes a free agent again. Plenty of coaches believe they can be the one to speak to a player’s better angels. As to Gardner-Johnson, the demons have won, far too often.

#2772. Atletico Madrid vs. Bayern Munich preview: Team news and predicted lineups

After being held to a 2-2 draw by Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga, an injury-hit Bayern Munich side turn their attention to Tuesday's trip to Spain to face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The Bavarians will be eager to return to winning ways in Europe's premier club competition, having drawn 3-3 against Viking FK and 2-2 with Arsenal in their last two Champions League outings. Those results have left them 14th in the league phase table with five points from three games.

However, Bayern face a tough test against Atletico Madrid, who are particularly strong at the Wanda Metropolitano, where they haven't lost since a 0-1 defeat to Celta Vigo in May last season.

A 1-1 Champions League draw against another Bundesliga side – VfB Stuttgart – was followed by domestic wins over Deportivo La Coruna (1-0) and Levante (2-0), giving Diego Simeone's men a positive run of results heading into Tuesday's clash. Atletico currently sit second in La Liga.

The two sides have met six times over the past 10 years, with Bayern winning three games, Atletico claiming two victories and one ending in a draw. Bayern have never beaten Atletico away from home and will be keen to change that on Tuesday.

Atletico Madrid will have to manage without Morten Hjulmand after he was shown a straight red card against Stuttgart. Johnny Cardoso (thigh) and Koke (muscle) are both doubts.

As for Bayern Munich, assistant coach Aaron Danks will continue deputising for head coach Vincent Kompany, who remains absent after collapsing and being diagnosed with meningeal irritation.

The German champions suffered a triple injury blow at the weekend, as Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all forced off during their 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund.

Saibari (ankle) and Gnabry (muscle) are both facing longer spells on the sidelines, but Olise could potentially feature after taking part in Bayern's final training session ahead of the game, albeit with his right knee bandaged.

Manuel Neuer also took part in the session and could return from a foot injury, with Jonas Urbig ready to deputise for the veteran goalkeeper once again if he is not passed fit.

Luis Diaz (muscle), Jamal Musiala (thigh) and Bara Sapoko Ndiaye (appendectomy) remain unavailable.

#2771. NFL trade deadline candidates include Derrick Henry and another Jets surprise

As the dust settles from this year's midterm elections, it's only natural to wonder if the NFL's trade deadline, which expires at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 10, will produce a "November surprise" or two of its own.

The New York Jets sprung two last year, unloading perceived cornerstone players Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams in separate transactions that netted three first-round picks, a second-rounder and WR Adonai Mitchell. The Gardner deal, in particular, wound up being something of a last gasp for the Indianapolis Colts under the stewardship of recently deposed GM Chris Ballard, who gave up two Round 1 selections and Mitchell in a swap that's already aged badly for Indy … though the Jets still have time screw it up on their end, too. But Mitchell and rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq have shown plenty of promise this season.

There's already been one stunner this fall after the Chicago Bears paid the hefty freight to liberate All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans – though he very much played like he was worth the two first-rounders he partially cost GM Ryan Poles during his highly effective debut in Seattle on Monday night.

We'll know in the coming days if another superstar unexpectedly gets a change-of-address notification. But here are 21 players – yes some may require suspension of disbelief to some degree, though none are outside the realm of possibility – to keep an eye on ahead of next week's cutoff:
